headline: Jeff Bezos’s Prometheus raises $12B for physical AI
summary: The AI startup, co-founded by Jeff Bezos, secured $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation to build an 'artificial general engineer' for physical systems.
details: Jeff Bezos's AI startup Prometheus has announced a massive $12 billion funding round, valuing the company at $41 billion. The funds were secured from a mix of investors including Bezos himself, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and BlackRock.

Prometheus aims to create an 'artificial general engineer,' a sophisticated AI software designed to automate the design and manufacturing processes for complex physical systems, ranging from jet engines to pharmaceutical compounds.

This substantial investment marks Prometheus's second funding round, following an initial $6.2 billion raise when it launched late last year. The company currently employs 150 individuals across its offices in San Francisco, London, and Zurich.

Bezos envisions this AI-driven automation will significantly boost productivity, potentially leading to a future with 'labor scarcity' where demand for human workers exceeds supply. He believes this will ultimately raise the standard of living, allowing for reduced working hours.

A significant portion of the newly raised capital will be allocated to the company's substantial compute infrastructure needs. This investment underscores the growing investor interest in the 'physical AI' sector, which is seen as more defensible than pure software due to real-world moats.
Prometheus's valuation places it among the most highly valued AI startups ever funded, signaling a major bet on the future of AI in physical engineering and manufacturing.

Jeff Bezos's AI startup Prometheus has announced a massive $12 billion funding round, valuing the company at $41 billion. The funds were secured from a mix of investors including Bezos himself, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and BlackRock.

Prometheus aims to create an 'artificial general engineer,' a sophisticated AI software designed to automate the design and manufacturing processes for complex physical systems, ranging from jet engines to pharmaceutical compounds.

This substantial investment marks Prometheus's second funding round, following an initial $6.2 billion raise when it launched late last year. The company currently employs 150 individuals across its offices in San Francisco, London, and Zurich.

Bezos envisions this AI-driven automation will significantly boost productivity, potentially leading to a future with 'labor scarcity' where demand for human workers exceeds supply. He believes this will ultimately raise the standard of living, allowing for reduced working hours.

A significant portion of the newly raised capital will be allocated to the company's substantial compute infrastructure needs. This investment underscores the growing investor interest in the 'physical AI' sector, which is seen as more defensible than pure software due to real-world moats.

Prometheus's valuation places it among the most highly valued AI startups ever funded, signaling a major bet on the future of AI in physical engineering and manufacturing.
